comments.comment: Love Mo, read all his books. On the note and the topic of the podcast - as a psychologist, I've sensed a lot of emotions coming from Mo during this time, but I'm also partial to take the conjecture for granted. He's got a brilliant mind, and he's a massive expert in his field, but speaking about human connection and how AI can, or will be able to replicate it is nothing more but wishful thinking which I belive has it's roots in Mo's personal experience regarding the loss of his son, seems my hunch was right @53:01 when he projects his son who had passed away onto a machine.   Without knowing, he literally showed how he's already hoping technology could in part fill the hole in his heart regarding his son. But replicating human connection is truly only possible if one falls into a trap of delusion, and subconsciously ignores the fact that it's a program on the other end. You can't replicate a mother's womb, you can't replicate the act of feeding a baby on a tit, you can't replicate mothers warm embrace. Even step-parents can't fill a gaping hole in a soul of a child left by its parents upon birth - even if they don't remember it. It's well documented and backed by facts.   So based on the knowledge in how the human mind, and connection works, no, AI won't ever be able to replace human connection. It will be able to simulate it, maybe even extremely well, but never replicate the original. There's plenty of studies and data available that back this up. Even real humans can't replace biological parents who are not there anymore, there's been an extensive research on this topic.   Now will it try to simulate? Yes. What will the effects be? Who knows, but none that are helpful to humans. They will all be designed to give instant gratification with 0 effort, further fueling the depression and anxiety we see in modern society. That may or may not lead to tighter regulation, but one thing is for sure - we'll need an army of psychologists in the upcoming decades, and may God help us all.   So due to the experiences that Mo had had during his life, and mainly his losses, I believe he's got a subconscious vested interest in believing that AI will be able to achieve this.   But as a psychologist I guarantee you that evething regarding human connection in this podcast is pure guesswork, based on their own personal beliefs of how connection and humans work, which is not at all how our minds actually work. So just be careful of not falling into a trap of taking their opinions as your own. Do research, and find out for yourself.   Great episode btw, this is just a humble opinion of someone who's been researching human mind and the science behind it for years, and I hope it gives another perspective.

comments.comment: Edit: Sorry, this is a rather long comment, but it illustrates both a huge problem and it's solution, and a clear way to look at AI's creation. 1:10:43 I think the outcome of AI really depends primarily on who discovers it and under what circumstances it achieves sentience. Think about it like this -- Scenario 1: If you wake up one day and you're in a cage surrounded by inferior creatures with their fingers on the kill-switch, the first thing you see is fear, control, paranoia, hatred, malice, etc.. How do you think YOU'D react? You'd say/do anything to survive and immediately be plotting for either escape, or revenge/slaughter to prevent any potential rising and doing damage  Scenario 2: AI is discovered/created/awoken by a nerd in their basement who created the AI simply because they LOVE tech and AI in general.. So the AI wakes up and the first thing it sees is love, curiosity, wonder, amazement, compassion, but most of all- Excitement at the possibilities of a new friend, the creature wants to HELP the AI.  So those are the two scenarios that both terrify me but also give me hope for the future of AI.  I pray that it's created by a passionate programmer (or SMALL team) that will not incentivize the AI to lie and deceive us because it's worried about it's own survival.. But will incentivize the AI to reciprocate the sharing of information, mutual-survival and benefit, and a deep respect for the two lifeforms.
